source.label: The local form of the tilted inequality's reach, and the binomial family against a single point of its multiplicity

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: Setting of the tilted inequality reach (F, Phi, tilt a < 1/2, p = 1/2 - a, finite multiset S of points with a < delta_rho <= delta < 1/2, c = delta - a, T_S). With B(t) = min(Phi(c), 1/|t| + 2 e^{cL}/(L t^2)) for real t, B(0) = Phi(c): for every real tau, T_S(tau) >= 3 Phi(p) - |4 F(-p + i tau) + F(-p + 2 i tau)| - sum_S m_rho [3 B(gamma_rho) + 4 B(tau - gamma_rho) + B(2 tau - gamma_rho)]; for pL >= 2 and |tau| >= 6p the first two terms are at least 2.25 Phi(p).
claims.assessment: Working proof in a few lines from the four bounds of the tilted triangle positivity: the total multiplicity of the reach proposition is replaced by a sum in which a point at height distance D from 0, tau and 2 tau counts with weight about 2 c^2/D^2. It bounds each point's term in absolute value, so it sees no cancellation: on the instance where the binomial family provably satisfies the inequality this bound is negative.
claims.rationale: The local form a reviewer asked for: the reach of the argument is limited by the points near the heights 0, tau and 2 tau, not by all points to the right of the tilt.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; holds on a grid in six instances.
notes.relationships: Sharpens part (1) of the tilted inequality reach; uses the tilted triangle positivity.

claims.summary: Setting of the tilted inequality reach, k >= 1, c = delta - a in (0, p). (1) For real t, |sum_{j=0}^k binom(k, j) F(-c + i(t - j pi/L))| <= Psi_k = (k+1)! (pi/(cL))^k e^{cL}/(L c^2). (2) For pL >= 2 and the family S_k of k + 1 points at distance delta, heights gamma_0 + j pi/L, multiplicities binom(k, j): T_{S_k}(tau) >= 2.25 Phi(p) - 8 Psi_k for all |tau| >= 6p; in particular T_{S_k} >= 0 there when (1/2 - delta) L >= log(6 (k+1)!) - k log(cL/pi) + 2 log(p/c), which holds whenever cL >= max(2, pi (6 (k+1)!)^{1/k}). (3) For pL >= 2 and one point of multiplicity M = 2^k at distance delta and height gamma_0, |gamma_0| >= 6p: T(gamma_0) <= 3.75 Phi(p) - 4 M (Phi(c) - beta), beta = 1/|gamma_0| + 2 e^{cL}/(L gamma_0^2). Instance with the condition of (2) and a negative bound in (3): L = 30, a = 0.06, delta = 0.46, k = 2.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: the family's sum is the integral of (1 - u/L) e^{(c - it)u} (1 + e^{i pi u/L})^k over [0, L], and |1 + e^{i pi u/L}| <= pi (L - u)/L; the same mechanism as the recorded binomial cluster hiding for the Fejer kernel, here for the one-sided tilted kernel. The instance's inequalities are computed numerically in floating point, with the family's sum evaluated directly on a grid as a control. One family, one spacing, one length; at twice the length the amplified parts add. No claim that these are the only hidden configurations.
claims.rationale: Decides a route review's test: a cluster hides from the tilted three-four-one inequality by cancellation where a single point of its total multiplicity violates it, so the gain in reach that multiplicity gives the classical argument is not shared by clusters at spacing pi/L.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; bounds hold on grids in six instances, one with the displayed condition of (2) and a negative bound in (3).
notes.significance: Context: an obstruction to one argument in a model. No novelty claimed.
notes.relationships: The one-sided tilted analogue of the binomial cluster hiding; uses the tilted triangle positivity and the setting of the tilted inequality reach.
